newsitem.title: USA: Marvel Entertainment files for Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: Marvel Entertainment files for Chapter 11.

text.p: Marvel Entertainment Group Inc said on Friday it filed a voluntary Chapter 11 petition for reorganization in a Delaware court.

The company said it filed the Chapter 11 petition to carry out a proposed $525 million recapitalization that would enable Marvel to pursue new strategic intiatives and achieve sustained profitability.

Marvel said the filing, in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware in Wilmington, Del., would ensure it could continue all business operations without interruption while it obtained necessary approval of its financial restructuring plan.

In a separate statement, Marvel Holdings, Marvel (Parent) Holdigns and Marvel III Holdings said on Friday they filed voluntary petitions for reorganization under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in a Delaware Court.
The three holding companies said they owned about 80.2 million shares of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc common stock. Financier Ronald Perelman's Andrews Group Inc controls Marvel.

Marvel Entertainment said the filing was necessitated by the failure of the holders of bonds issued by Marvel's holding companies to reach agreement regarding any alternative plans for the company's future.
Marvel Entertainment has $229.6 million in assets and $693.2 million in liabilities, according to court papers.
Of those liabilities, $630.7 million is contingent secured debt and $58.2 million is fixed liquidated unsecured debt, according to court papers.

The Wall Street Journal reported on November 22 that Perelman's representatives warned Marvel Entertainment bondholders that Marvel would be forced to file for protection in bankruptcy court unless they approved a reorganization plan to massively dilute stockholders ownership position.

The newspaper cited an analyst who attended a private meeting between the two groups as saying the representatives presented documents showing that Marvel's four main operating business would together report $100 million less in revenue in 1996 than in 1995.
It said the documents also showed that three of the businesses would report operating losses.

Marvel said that as a result of Friday's petition, it would be able to avail itself of the processes of the court to complete the reorganization and move forward without the necessity of bondholder consent.

"We would have preferred to re-capitalize Marvel without having to seek the aid of the court, but the actions and positions taken by the bondholders prevented that approach," said Scott Sassa, chairman and chief executive of Marvel.

The company said it intended to pay all of its bills, including those submitted before the filing, on time and in full, and maintain normal credit terms with suppliers and licensors. It also said it expected to continue doing business with our customers and licensees under normal business terms.

Marvel said its strategic investment program included Marvel Studios' development of television and film properties, Marvel Mania theme restaurants, Marvel Interactive software and Fleer/SkyBox trading card initiatives.
Under the proposed financial restructuring plan, Marvel said Andrews Group would invest $365 million in new equity in Marvel, allowing Marvel to make Toy Biz Inc a wholly-owned subsidiary of Marvel.
In turn, Marvel said its lender group has agreed to provide $160 million in new funds to finance Marvel's new strategic investment program and working capital requirements.
Marvel said its board had approved this proposed plan.
In conjunction with the Chapter 11 filing, Marvel said a bank group led by Chase Manhattan Bank agreed to provide Marvel with $100 million of debtor-in- possession financing.

Upon court approval, which the company said it expected shortly, this financing would ensure Marvel had sufficient liquidity to pay all current and expected trade and employee obligations and to meet all of its operating and investment needs during the reorganization process, the company said.
Marvel said it expected the reorganization to be completed within a few months, although there could be no assurance.
